patient.chief_complaint: Sudden severe headache, told it may be her IIH acting up
patient.history_present_illness: Ms. Tanaka is a 44-year-old nurse with known idiopathic intracranial hypertension who presents with a sudden onset severe headache that began 4 hours ago. She reports headaches are common for her due to her IIH, but this headache was distinctly different: it came on instantaneously and reached maximum intensity within 2-3 seconds, whereas her typical IIH headaches build over 15-30 minutes. She rates it 10/10 vs her typical IIH headaches which are usually 5-7/10. She has photophobia and neck stiffness, which she says is unusual for her IIH. She initially contacted her neurology nurse line and was told her IIH might be flaring and to increase acetazolamide. However, a supervising neurologist (who was covering) insisted she come to the ED. As a nurse herself, she is extremely worried about SAH but also thinks it might just be IIH. The diagnostic challenge: 1) IIH patient with chronically elevated ICP may have higher baseline CSF pressure, making LP interpretation more complex; 2) IIH headaches can be severe; 3) IIH can mask or complicate SAH diagnosis.

output.query: Idiopathic intracranial hypertension SAH co-occurrence LP interpretation

results.finding: IIH and SAH are distinct conditions that can co-occur - thunderclap onset should always prompt SAH workup
LP in IIH: elevated opening pressure but CLEAR CSF without xanthochromia unless SAH has occurred
Spectrophotometry is essential to distinguish IIH LP (clear, no xanthochromia) from SAH LP (xanthochromic)
IIH elevated ICP may worsen outcome in SAH by reducing cerebral perfusion pressure

output.summary: IIH patients have chronically elevated ICP with clear CSF. When SAH occurs, CSF becomes bloody/xanthochromic - clearly different from IIH LP. Spectrophotometry is the discriminating test. Chronic elevated ICP from IIH may worsen SAH outcomes by reducing CPP. Acetazolamide should be assessed in context of acute SAH management priorities.

warnings: Monitor CPP = MAP - ICP; in IIH patient with elevated baseline ICP, maintain MAP higher to ensure adequate CPP >70

Target MAP >90 given estimated ICP 35-42 cmH2O
